name: Howard City Campground
note: Pull-through cement pads on the north side of SD-34 at the east edge of town; reserve with the city office by phone or email. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: City of Howard campground page (cityofhoward.com, Community Amenities > Campground, read 2026-11-22): 'The Howard City Campground includes 7 cement camping pads with water, electric and sewer hookups ... All sites are 50 amps and are pull through accessible. The campground is located along Hwy 34, just east of the Howard Community Fire Hall. Camping fees are $22 per night. For reservations contact the City Office' -> real drive-in RV campground a 23-ft rig fits (pull-throughs; imagery shows the angled pads ~15+ m long). Currently operating: Campendium review 2026-06-20 (2 nights, site 1, travel trailer, $22/night, 'call for reservations'). Town park: no price gate, the city page is the presence. Not in the DB: no entry named Howard in SD and nothing within 20 km (nearest 13156 Lake Carthage LUA, 23 km).
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-22: Esri World Imagery at 44.0108,-97.5265 (2.4 km frame), 44.0080,-97.5240 (600 m) and 44.00855,-97.5214 (240 m); all three images rendered. The pads sit on a gravel loop on mown grass between SD-34 and houses at the east edge of Howard; no water in the 600 m frame. Nearest water is a small creek channel ~0.6 km east (crossing SD-34 at the town's east edge) and a farm pond ~0.75 km SE, neither visible or reachable from the sites -> not waterfront.
fees_source: https://www.cityofhoward.com/index.asp?SEC=08E8D9D5-B0E5-4D7E-9B86-A562E4C800FE (read 2026-11-22): 'Camping fees are $22 per night.' Corroborated by a Campendium review dated 2026-06-20 ('$22/night', site 1); a 2020 review paid $18.

facilities_source: https://www.cityofhoward.com/index.asp?SEC=08E8D9D5-B0E5-4D7E-9B86-A562E4C800FE (read 2026-11-22): 'A new restroom facility, complete with showers, was completed in 2006.'
flags: Pin placed on the angled pads seen in Esri imagery north of SD-34 at the east edge of town (Campendium's point 44.009,-97.522 is ~35 m north, consistent). Imagery shows ~6-8 angled pads along a gravel loop with a small red-roofed building (likely the restroom) - matches the city's 7 pads, but nothing on imagery labels it, so the reviewer may want a glance.
